question:
Segment \(BD\) and \(AE\) intersect at \(C,\) as shown, \(AB=BC=CD=CE,\) and \(\angle A=\dfrac52\angle B.\) What is the degree measure of \(\angle D?\)

[Figure 1](figures/2009_AMC_10B_Q09_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
The equal sides identify equal angles in both triangles. In \(\triangle ABC\), the condition \(AB=BC\) gives
\[
\angle BAC=\angle ACB.
\]
Let \(x\) be the degree measure of \(\angle ABC\). The given angle relationship makes each of the other two angles \(\frac52x\) degrees. The triangle angle sum therefore gives
\[
x+\frac52x+\frac52x=180,
\]
so \(6x=180\) and \(x=30\). Hence \(\angle ACB=75^\circ\).

Because \(AE\) and \(BD\) intersect at \(C\), angles \(ACB\) and \(DCE\) are vertical angles. Thus \(\angle DCE=75^\circ\). In \(\triangle CDE\), the condition \(CD=CE\) gives equal angles at \(D\) and \(E\). Each is therefore
\[
\frac{180^\circ-75^\circ}{2}=52.5^\circ.
\]
Thus \(\angle D=\boxed{52.5^\circ}\), choice A.
